lesson: Listen to where it starts. Not with a thought. Not with the poet telling you anything. It starts with two smells. Coffee grounds and wood smoke before you're even fully awake. That's smart. The nose remembers before the head does, so the poem enters through the body and earns your trust before it asks you to feel anything. Watch how the images hand off. The scent becomes the turn shoulder of the year. Then the mug in your hands. Then the maple rusting at its edges. And notice that rust is a slow burn. Quiet destruction that's also beautiful. Then it moves indoors to that sealed jar. Proof your hands were here. Everything's still a picture. The turn comes at they add up quiet the way a season does. That's where the jars and hours stop being objects and become a life being counted. Here's the thing to steal. Let a plain object carry the feeling. The sealed jar does the poem's emotional work without one word about pride. I'll let you find what those last two lines are doing.
